{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -J pi_monte_carlo
#   -o pi_monte_carlo.out
#   -e pi_monte_carlo.err
#   -p test
#   -t 30
#   -n 8
#   --mem-per-cpu=4000

flux alloc \
  -n 8 \
  --time=30m \
  --queue=test \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm stdout/stderr files
exec >pi_monte_carlo.out 2>pi_monte_carlo.err

# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=4000 has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm job name (-J pi_monte_carlo) is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# NOTE: Slurm used srun --mpi=pmix for MPI bootstrap. Flux MPI integration is site-specific;
# there is no portable equivalent to "--mpi=pmix" here.
# Performance implication: MPI startup may fail or perform differently unless your environment provides
# an MPI launcher compatible with Flux.

module load intel/24.0.1-fasrc01 openmpi/5.0.2-fasrc01

# Best-effort: run with mpirun using the requested task count.
mpirun -np 8 ./pi_monte_carlo.x
'
"
}
